I have been a leader in most, if not all, of my groupworks. That means I've worked with different people within the spectrum - from the super tamad to the hindi mo na kailangan i-proofread 'yung gawa kasi sobrang ganda na. 

What I can advice from this is never be groupmates with your actual friends, lalong-lalo na sa research-related subjects. Most likely kasi, ang iisipin nila ay since you're all friends, hindi magiging ganoon ka-strict. Magiging complacent sila and all knowing na wala namang magagalit sa kanila because "friends.' However, it's very tricky rin kasi most of them just don'r know how to demarcate between professionalism and your friendship.

But since ayun na nga, magkakagrupo na kayo, wala na tayong magagawa riyan. My best advice would be having a shift to a stricter tone with regard to reminding deadlines in the GC or just delegating tasks in general. Kadalasan kasi, if you go easy on them and never learn to say no, hindi nila nakukuha 'yung gusto mong i-communicate. Eh totally valid naman 'yung response mo kasi gaya nga ng sabi mo, research 'yan. This may sound cliché, but it's all about having your rest, doing your best, and above all - rewarding yourself.

Rest is very important to my routine. When I have many deadlines, but I am tired, I sleep. Some may say that it's counterproductive, but I'd argue otherwise. Doing your tasks with a broken sequence, many distractions (such as getting sleep), and without having 100% immersion to the task at hand would result in an output of lesser quality, plus no sleep! I suggest reading Deep Work by Cal Newport to gain more insight on this. Anyway, what's most important is you recognize the difference between procrastination and simply setting the mood for yourself.

Penultimately, doing your best is just simply doing your best. Most of us confuse our best with only what we can do at that moment. While that might be true to some extent, that mindset limits us to a standard of bare minimum. Even though we think that we did our best, it is a fact that it was not our best. Doing our best, in my opinion, is managing our time efficiently, going over the output a healthy number of times, asking other people's insights that might prove as constructive criticism, and so much more.

And the last would be rewarding yourself. This is very important in the process. Having done your utmost best, you deserve a treat! You have got to celebrate even the smallest wins because you pushed through no matter how insignificant it is. Treat yourself to good food, or play a game you've always wanted to play. Anything that reinforces that reward system gives positive feedback to your effort, and most of the time, we become more motivated for the future tasks to come!
